pr_title: Refactor apiserver endpoint transformers to more natively use Encoders
pr_body:
Fix https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/83898

This PR on its own addresses the above issue.
But its main purpose is to enable a large memory allocation optimization:
- in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/1152-less-object-serializations we created a framework and avoided serializing the same object multiple times
- however, there is one big piece that I missed:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/watch.go#L274-L290
- even though the serialization of watch-event is simple [we just copy bytes around], we're allocating quite a bit of memory there and optimizing that can bring non-negligible savings
- this PR [in addition to being a nice cleanup on its own] enables that improvement in a clear way

```release-note
NONE
```

To reviewers: I recommend reviewing commit-by-commit - commits are self-contained and build on top of each other.

/kind cleanup
/priority important-longterm
/sig api-machinery

issue_context.title: Refactor transformObject to implement Encoder interface
issue_context.body:
Long-term, transformObject:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5219ad7be209b31cdfdae2eda1cd435aff4a3cd2/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/response.go#L40
should be refactored so that it implements Encoder interface (and it has nested encoder inside):

This would allow us to cache the results for difference media.Convert options, which currently is not supported:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5219ad7be209b31cdfdae2eda1cd435aff4a3cd2/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/response.go#L50

@kubernetes/sig-api-machinery-misc @liggitt
comments: To implement Encoder interface, the negotiation.MediaTypeOptions would be passed to the class where transformation code (Encode()) resides, right ?
Let us know if you need help

I won't get to it any time soon TBH. So marking lifecycle frozen for now.

/lifecycle frozen

review_comments: add a comment to the target == nil case in `doTransformObject` that if we ever change that from a no-op, this needs to update to include whatever variable behavior we have
I recommend reviewing commit-by-commit - commits are self-contained and build on top of each other.

move this to transformResponseObject rather than narrowly to ListResource / DeleteCollection so we keep handling this correctly for custom API servers that return list types from subresources or other verb handlers
let's also document doTransformObject is used for all responses, including watch streams, and document transformResponseObject is only used for non-streaming responses
just to sanity check, maybe put a println here and make sure we're still actually making use of this (or skip this block unconditionally and see if a unit test fails)

I tested that against some integration tests with the following diff:
```
diff --git a/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/watch.go b/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/watch.go
index ab874e30bfe..45bf5be20b4 100644
--- a/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/watch.go
+++ b/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/watch.go
@@ -34,6 +34,8 @@ import (
        "k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/negotiation"
        "k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/metrics"
        apirequest "k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/request"
+
+       "k8s.io/klog/v2"
 )
 
 // nothing will ever be sent down this channel
@@ -113,6 +115,7 @@ func serveWatch(watcher watch.Interface, scope *RequestScope, mediaTypeOptions n
                // instead, we allocate the buffer for the entire watch session and release it when we close the connection.
                memoryAllocator = runtime.AllocatorPool.Get().(*runtime.Allocator)
                defer runtime.AllocatorPool.Put(memoryAllocator)
+               klog.Errorf("MEMORY_ALOCATOR: embedded encoder")
                embeddedEncoder = runtime.NewEncoderWithAllocator(encoderWithAllocator, memoryAllocator)
        }
        if tableOptions, ok := options.(*metav1.TableOptions); ok {
@@ -128,6 +131,7 @@ func serveWatch(watcher watch.Interface, scope *RequestScope, mediaTypeOptions n
                        memoryAllocator = runtime.AllocatorPool.Get().(*runtime.Allocator)
                        defer runtime.AllocatorPool.Put(memoryAllocator)
                }
+               klog.Errorf("MEMORY_ALOCATOR: encoder")
                encoder = runtime.NewEncoderWithAllocator(encoderWithAllocator, memoryAllocator)
        }
```

It works as expected.
